metric_definition.reference: NumPy float64 unscaled FFT of exact signed Q15 integer codes
metric_definition.unit: one signed input-component integer code equals one input LSB
metric_definition.rms: sqrt(mean(component_error_squared)) over the pooled component population
metric_definition.scaled_candidates: metrics are calculated after restoring the candidate scale/exponent

candidate_arithmetic.downstream_power_consequence: wide exact-square candidate; power width remains unfrozen

candidate_arithmetic.error_interpretation: A 13-bit right shift has an 8192-input-LSB quantization step after scale restoration; ties-to-even rounding therefore permits the observed half-step 4096-LSB maximum error.
candidate_arithmetic.downstream_power_consequence: narrower payload but fixed normalization dependency

candidate_arithmetic.error_interpretation: Frames using exponent 13 have an 8192-input-LSB restored quantization step; the observed 4096-LSB maximum is its half-step rounding bound, not overflow or wrap.
candidate_arithmetic.downstream_power_consequence: per-frame exponent must accompany power and detector state

phase_factor_planning_criterion.origin: PHASE-06C architecture-selection planning baseline; not a pre-existing repository acceptance gate
phase_factor_planning_criterion.scope: architectural radix-2 proxy only; real AMD C-model acceptance remains future work

selection_reason: Unscaled full precision preserves the PHASE-02 normalization relationship and deterministic Q15 binary point; 29-bit components cover the vendor full-precision growth rule. A 24-bit phase factor materially reduces the architectural proxy error without imposing the 32-bit candidate width.
vendor_accuracy_boundary: Actual AMD numerical behavior remains unproven until matching C-model/XSim execution.
